seam_mechanism: cement solvent weld or pressure-sensitive tape splice
joint_inspectable_by: loupe — the splice is visible as a physical object
failure_when_botched: Localized thickness at the join causes gate flutter or lost loop tension at 24fps. Over-scraped emulsion prints as a white flash across the frame line; under-scraped emulsion snaps under tension.
source_note: A/B rolling hid the splice by checkerboarding the negative across two reels interleaved with black leader, so the physical join sat under unexposed stock on the opposite roll.

seam_mechanism: razor cut along the guard band between vertical sync pulses; later electronic assemble and insert edits
clearance_is_in_band: yes — the control track is in the signal
joint_inspectable_by: ferrofluid under a microscope — iron powder in solvent renders the magnetic track visible
failure_when_botched: Cutting at the wrong angle splits a vertical sync pulse and the monitor loses field lock, rolling or tearing. Electronic punch-in without PLL lockup writes a burst of high-frequency noise at the seam.
source_note: Quadruplex heads scan transversely across the tape width, not diagonally — diagonal scan is helical, which arrived later with Type C and the cassette formats. The guard-band cut and the ferrofluid technique are as described.

seam_mechanism: a mathematical point on a timeline, HH:MM:SS:FF
state_cleared: not applicable — sources are discrete files
joint_inspectable_by: the edit decision list — the cut is a line of text
failure_when_botched: A hard cut in digital audio is a sample-level amplitude discontinuity and reads as a click. NLEs place a sub-frame equal-power crossfade of roughly 2-5ms across the visual cut.
source_note: Avid Media Composer and Lightworks were competing systems from different companies, not one product. The seam here becomes psychological — the 180-degree rule, cutting on action, and J/L cuts are all techniques for hiding a join that costs nothing to make.

seam_mechanism: a forced IDR frame at the cut point
state_cleared: yes — the decoded picture buffer is flushed and all prior temporal references discarded
clearance_is_in_band: yes — the IDR is a syntax element in the bitstream
joint_inspectable_by: bitstream inspection — the NAL unit type is readable
failure_when_botched: Cutting on a non-keyframe boundary without re-encoding applies scene B's motion vectors to scene A's residual pixels. The result is smearing and macroblock artifacts.
source_note: This is the era that solved the problem the generative era reopened. An IDR is an explicit, in-band, machine-checkable instruction to discard state at a discontinuity.

seam_mechanism: none — the model interpolates because interpolation is its only mode
joint_inspectable_by: nothing — a morph and a cut are both just pixels
failure_when_botched: Prompted across a scene change, a diffusion model morphs, melts or warps A into B. A hard cut breaks its cross-frame attention and it resolves the contextual rupture with hallucinated noise or ghost frames. In a sliding autoregressive window, prior latents pull the new scene back toward the old, corrupting lighting, geometry and character.
source_note: The regression is specific: era 4 had an in-band clearance instruction and era 5 does not. Everything H.SYN.EMA adds at the seam is an attempt to restore what the IDR frame already established, in a medium where the artifact is a probability sample rather than a decodable stream.
